literal: On smelling, will wither the Aniccham flower; face having changed, on looking, will wither the guest.
translation: The delicate Aniccham flower withers merely by being smelled; likewise, a guest's heart withers the moment one's face changes and looks away.
modern: அனிச்சப் பூ மோந்து பார்த்தாலே வாடிவிடும்; அதுபோல, முகம் வேறுபட்டுப் பார்ப்பதைக் கண்டவுடனேயே விருந்தினர் வாடிவிடுவர்.
explanation: The poet compares the delicate nature of a guest to the legendary Aniccham flower. While the Aniccham flower is so sensitive that it withers merely upon being smelled, a guest is even more sensitive, drooping the moment they notice a cold change in the host's facial expression. This emphasizes that true hospitality is not just about providing food, but about maintaining a warm, welcoming countenance. Even a slight, silent shift in the host's face can deeply hurt a guest's feelings.
